_about: Enemies inside a skirmish. Numbers are in tens. Enemy damage is static and telegraphed exactly; only the player's kinetic faces roll. rank is where they prefer to stand: front foes step up, back foes hold. size 2 is massive and fills both slots of a column. armour (default 0) comes off every blow that lands on the foe, flat, never off a burn. stun_resist (default 0) is the foe's base chance, percent, to shrug off a suppress; Numbed adds 10 a stack on top and decays a stack each turn; bosses carry 30 as a placeholder (26 September). aim (decided 2 October; default exposed) is the sense the foe's target pick follows, each foe on its own as the round opens, shown as its arrow before the player acts: exposed (weighted toward the machine its blows would hurt most: the hull they reach plus half of any shield they break), anything (any machine alike), heat (the hottest machine), armed (a machine showing an intact weapon), focus (the rank shares one pick). A move may carry its own aim. Player-facing text: codex (what the codex says), flavour (an in-world quote, shown in italics), and each action's text. design is internal and never shown: fantasy (the pitch, inspiration, homages), niche (the tactical problem the foe poses), notes. actions is the foe's roster of moves, each kind attack, defend, buff or debuff, with status implemented or planned; only implemented actions appear in the codex. Rank and file have one or two moves, a boss three, the third a signature that opens on a condition. A move may carry when, one word or a list meaning any, the condition that lets the foe pick it this round (below_half, missing_hull: missing at least its value, few_waiting: fewer than two of the foe it summons wait, rerolls_left: the team has rerolls to lose, machine_hot: a machine carries 20 heat or more, machine_armed: a machine shows an intact weapon, back_behind: a back-rank foe stands behind it, others_on_field: another foe stands with it); a move whose condition fails is not rolled, and a special never fires twice running when anything else is open. A defend, buff or debuff action names an effect the engine runs (Foe.ACTION_EFFECTS: harden with value, regrow with value; revive_once, summon with foe and count, rally with value; drain_rerolls, add_heat, scramble, crack, disable, heat_all, corrupt_all) and is picked by weight like an attack, in place of a blow that turn. Write {value} in its text for its number. Component injuries are a global rule, not a foe property. On the map (decided 1 October): zone is the pack's engagement zone in hexes (default 1), the radius around where it ends its move inside which every machine fights it; behaviour is how its pack moves: push (default; the gate, its path committed when the round opens), aggressive (the gate, unless a machine ends within its reach, its move plus its zone, in which case it comes for the biggest catch it can make) or hunt (locks one machine when it spawns and chases it until one of them is dead); hunts is a hunter's caveat for picking that machine: nearest (default), weakest, strongest, slowest or fastest; movespeed is its move in tens (default 20): a pack pays 10 for any land hex and never enters water or a crag (the horde flattens what it crosses; the Final Fantasy overworld rule, Ryan, 2 October), so its reach is a plain ring bent only round water and rock; bosses patrol at 10. An implemented attack action scales the base attack: factor (default 1.0; damage is attack times factor, rounded), strikes (default 1; each a separate blow, so a double strike breaks a shield and reaches the hull), swarm (so much more damage per other foe of its type on the field: the ghoul's threat is its numbers), keywords (tags on the blow; breach: its blows overflow shield into hull and can injure through it, dangerous and uncommon; scorch: a stack of Overheating on the machine hit; disable and corrupt act on the entry the machine's die shows), weight (default 1; attacks weigh 2 to a special's 1 among the moves whose conditions hold). Write {damage} in an action's text and the resulting number is shown. Foes stand and strike front rank left to right then back rank; the heaviest hitters deploy left. Numbers are placeholders, the set of 2 October written for play testing (the bible, section 9).

entries.name: Ghoul

design.fantasy: A body that forgot to stop.
design.niche: There are six of them and four slots. Kill fast or be buried: every one standing makes every other one hit harder.
design.notes: The swarm claw since 2 October (Ryan: the revive was confusing; a smaller monster's threat is its numbers): 5, and 5 more for every other ghoul on the field, so four on the field hit for 20 each and killing one drops every blow. One move, so a disrupt has nothing to switch it to. Get Back Up is gone from it; the necromancer is the Risen's "hard to keep down" now. Aims at anything.

entries.codex: The rank and file of the Risen. Slow, stupid and never alone: six arrive for every one you put down, and they walk straight at the nearest thing with a heartbeat. The more of them stand, the harder each one hits.

actions.name: Claw
actions.text: Tears at anything in reach for {damage}: more for every other ghoul standing.

entries.flavour: They don't run. They don't have to. You'll get tired first.

entries.name: Necromancer

design.fantasy: The reason the ghouls keep coming.
design.niche: It hides behind the wall and keeps the wall standing. Reach it, or chew through.
design.notes: Raise runs since 30 September (summon); since 2 October it fires only when fewer than two ghouls wait, and the back rank fires as one (aim focus), so the casters coordinate while the bodies flail.

entries.codex: Keeps to the back rank behind a wall of ghouls and keeps the wall standing. Anything that can reach past the front is worth more here than anywhere else.

actions.name: Hex Bolt
actions.text: A bolt of grave-light for {damage}.

actions.name: Raise
actions.text: Calls a ghoul up from the pool at the end of the round.

entries.flavour: Kill the one doing the talking.

entries.name: Brute

design.niche: Its swing is telegraphed. Shield for it, suppress it, or disrupt it into a roar once the rerolls are spent.
design.notes: Roar runs since 30 September (drain_rerolls); since 2 October only when the team has rerolls to lose, and never twice running. Aims at the exposed.

entries.codex: A slab of muscle that swings once a round and means it. Everything it does is announced a round early, which is the only reason anyone survives it.

actions.name: Haymaker
actions.text: One enormous swing for {damage}.

actions.name: Roar
actions.text: Costs the team one reroll next round.

entries.flavour: Big, loud and honest. I've fought worse people.

entries.name: Hellcaster

design.niche: Heat from the back rank: the bolt scorches and the stoke finishes it. Lure it onto a cold machine, suppress it, or reach it with indirect fire.
design.notes: Since 2 October the bolt is 20 with Scorch (it was a plain 30) so the heat is the rider, and Stoke aims at heat and fires only when a machine carries 20 or more, so it finishes a hot machine rather than warming a cold one.

entries.codex: Infernal artillery. Stands at the back and lobs fire over the front rank; the front rank exists so it can. What it hits runs hot, and it knows where the heat is.

actions.name: Firebolt
actions.text: Lobbed fire for {damage}, over the front rank. It scorches.

actions.name: Stoke
actions.text: Adds {value} heat to the hottest machine.

entries.flavour: If the sky turns orange, that's not the sunset.

entries.name: Spawn

design.niche: Unremarkable alone. Exists to shield the whisperer, and hardens when it is doing that job or when it is hurt. Hit the other column, or hit it once and hard.
design.notes: Fold runs since 30 September; flat armour since 2 October (harden +10), when a back-rank foe stands behind it or it is below half.

entries.codex: Something like a body, folded wrong. Harmless enough on its own; in numbers it is a wall that keeps the Whisperer out of reach, and it folds tighter when something stands behind it.

actions.name: Lash
actions.text: A limb from an unexpected direction for {damage}.

actions.name: Fold
actions.text: Folds in on itself: armour +{value} until its next action.

entries.flavour: Count the limbs. Now count again.

entries.name: Whisperer

design.niche: It goes for the loaded gun: its hits corrupt what you rolled and its hush switches it off. Redundancy wins; so does showing it a blank or a shield.
design.notes: Since 2 October: Murmur carries Corrupt and Hush switches off the showing entry (disable) when a machine shows an intact weapon; both aim at the armed. The spoiled reroll (scramble) is gone from it: one foe doing two things to the die is the act, and the reroll was the less readable.

entries.codex: It does not hit hard. It hits your dice. A machine that has been whispered to does not roll what was installed, and a machine that shows it a loaded gun finds the gun switched off.

actions.name: Murmur
actions.text: A word that hurts, for {damage}, and corrupts the component the machine is showing.

actions.name: Hush
actions.text: Switches off the weapon one mech's die is showing, through its next turn.

entries.flavour: Your die came up with a face you never fitted. Don't trust it. Don't trust the next one either.

entries.name: Bone Colossus

design.fantasy: A cathedral of ribs that walks.
design.niche: Fills a whole column. Nothing behind it is reachable until it falls, and it does not fall quickly: burst and burn against the knitting, armour against the storm.
design.notes: Massive boss. On the battlefield it is a three-hex unit. Knit runs since 30 September (regrow); since 2 October only when missing 20 or more. Armour 10. The third move, Bone Storm, opens below half: three blows of 10 at anything, the volume answer to a machine that armoured for the sweep.

entries.codex: A cathedral of ribs that walks. Fills a whole column; nothing behind it can be reached until it falls, and it does not fall quickly. Hurt it badly enough and the ribs start to fly.

actions.name: Sweep
actions.text: A rib the size of a girder, for {damage}.

actions.name: Knit
actions.text: Regrows {value} hull.

actions.name: Bone Storm
actions.text: Ribs fly: three blows of {damage} at anything.

entries.flavour: Gate order four still applies. Bring more gun.

entries.name: Pit Lord

design.niche: The biggest telegraphed hit in the game, and it breaches, so no shield answers it: suppress it, lure it onto hull that can take it, or disrupt it into a Kindle when another demon stands.
design.notes: Massive boss. Furnace Blow carries Breach since 2 October. Kindle runs since 30 September (rally); since 2 October only when another demon stands, so it never rallies an empty field. Armour 10. The third move, Eruption, opens below half: 10 heat to every machine.

entries.codex: The furnace has a face. The single biggest telegraphed hit in the campaign, every round, until it is dead, and a shield does not stop it. When it is hurt the furnace vents on everyone.

actions.name: Furnace Blow
actions.text: A fist of slag for {damage}, through the shield.

actions.name: Kindle
actions.text: Every other demon on the field hits {value} harder next round.

actions.name: Eruption
actions.text: The furnace vents: {value} heat to every machine.

entries.flavour: They brought fire. We brought bigger fire. It brought the biggest.

entries.name: The Maw

design.fantasy: You do not see all of it. That is a mercy.
design.niche: Bites twice a round at whoever shows it a weapon, and cracks what it sees. Redundancy wins; burst loses; a blank or a shield showing is a kind of armour.
design.notes: Massive boss. Bite strikes twice since 2 October and aims at the armed, like Unmake (crack, since 30 September; since 2 October only when a machine shows an intact component). Armour 10. The third move, Unravel, opens below half: every machine's showing component corrupted.

entries.codex: You do not see all of it. The part you can see bites twice, at whatever is pointing a gun at it, and what it bites cracks. Hurt it and everything you rolled goes wrong at once.

actions.name: Bite
actions.text: The visible part closes, twice, for {damage} each.

actions.name: Unmake
actions.text: Cracks the component one mech's die is showing, no hull hit needed.

actions.name: Unravel
actions.text: Everything you rolled is wrong: every machine's showing component is corrupted.

entries.flavour: Appendix K, last page: if you can read this, it hasn't noticed you yet.
